sections.html:
Suite A102 at 1903 Marquette Avenue, Muskegon, MI 49442, is where Muskegon County deeds are filed, and 231-724-6271 reaches the staff. The office is staffed weekdays, 8 a.m. through 5 p.m., though anything meant for the record has to arrive by 4:30 p.m.

Besides deeds, the office keeps mortgages, liens, surveys, plats, land contracts, condominium filings and financing statements. The same counter collects state and county transfer tax when the deed is recorded.

Writing or advising on a deed is off limits, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from legal advice. Owners are pointed to title companies, real estate lawyers or off-the-shelf forms that satisfy the state's recording standards.

You may file at the counter, by mail or online, as long as the paper bears original signatures. Photocopies and faxes come back unrecorded.

E-filing runs through CSC, EPN, Indecomm or Simplifile. A few kinds of documents must still come on paper.

  • Master deeds, and amendments that change a legal description and bring large drawings.
  • Plats.
  • Property transfer affidavits, which go to the equalization department instead.

Ask your title company which of these vendors, if any, it uses. When mailing, include the original deed, the fee check or checks, and a note listing your phone number so staff can reach you if the paper is returned.

The office adds two free protections. Home Security Search lets an owner look up records under their own name, and Fraud Guard emails you when your name shows up on a document headed for recording in the county. Both suit a landlord or an owner who holds property for years, and a seller can turn the alert on before listing to watch for odd filings.

Within the $30 recording charge, $4 funds the state's survey and remonumentation program. A warranty deed, land contract or other deed with a covenant of warranty also needs a treasurer's tax certificate.

Muskegon County register of deeds charges

If you pay by check and need a certificate, write two: one to the register of deeds for recording and transfer tax, the other for $5 to the Muskegon County Treasurer.

sections.h2: Taxes the seller owes at recording
sections.html:
Two taxes land on the grantor: $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on every $500 block of the price. A leftover partial block is charged as a full one, which nudges the bill up slightly. Both are paid at the register's counter along with the recording fee.

Distressed sales are handled differently. A sheriff's deed always escapes the state tax and only sometimes escapes the county tax. The state act also exempts deeds given in foreclosure or in place of it, and both acts exempt a corrective deed and a spousal conveyance that makes or ends a tenancy by the entirety. Whichever exemption fits, the deed itself must carry the wording.

First comes the treasurer's stamp, proof that the parcel's taxes are current. No warranty deed gets recorded without it, so any balance due is paid off by closing.

The loan is next. A payoff leads the lender to record a discharge, and no new deed is issued. Copies of the discharge or of your deed can be bought at the counter or through the online record search.

  • Pull the current deed so the legal description is copied word for word.
  • List every owner by exact name, since a missing owner means a missing signature.
  • Record a certified death certificate or proof of death if the deed names a survivor.
  • Get the clerk's certification and seal on any court order.

Removing or adding a name takes a new, notarized deed, not an amendment. Recording a certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a fresh deed. A title company or attorney should prepare the paper, and you should expect to sign in front of a notary. Double-check each owner's name against the earlier deed before signing.

Equalization, the county department, keeps the property forms. The transfer affidavit travels from the new owner to the city or township assessor, and an owner who lives in the home can claim the principal residence exemption from up to 18 mills of school operating tax. Other hardship relief is requested at the local assessor. Some cities and townships are assessed by the county, while the rest keep their own assessors.

If you claimed the principal residence exemption as a seller, ask the local assessor how to rescind it once you move out. Keep the confirmation with your sale papers. The buyer's new exemption and the transfer affidavit are separate filings, so each side should confirm theirs was received.

Most of Muskegon County by area is water: 961 of 1,460 square miles are lake, leaving 499 square miles of dry ground. Muskegon Lake is Michigan's only deep water port on Lake Michigan, and White Lake and Mona Lake add more shoreline. The urban southwest corner holds Muskegon, Muskegon Heights, Roosevelt Park and Norton Shores.

Muskegon County counted 175,824 people in 2020 and an estimated 177,901 in July 2025. Owners live in 78.1% of housing units, median home value stands at $198,300 and median rent is $1,028. Builders took out 451 permits in 2025.

Heavy lake-effect snow each winter leads buyers of older homes to ask about roofs and porches, so have repair records ready. Beaches and bike trails shape how buyers value a lakeside address. A cottage-style house near Pere Marquette Beach or Mona Lake often draws different offers than a mid-century house inland, so a seller should pin down the parcel's legal description and township before listing.

The buyer files the property transfer affidavit with the assessor. From the day the deed hits the record, your homestead-type exemptions are over and the new owner has to claim fresh ones. If you still owe back taxes, ask the treasurer what the payoff is a few days ahead; the title company will send it from the money you receive.

All-cash purchasers who accept the home as is must still get the tax certificate, a notary signature and the recording done. Ask how long each takes before you pick a closing date.

The register accepts new papers only until 4:30 p.m. If the lender wires funds after that, the deed is filed the following morning, so tell your closing agent about the cutoff. When the deed is indexed, buy a copy at the counter for $1 a page or print one from the online search, and put it in your closing folder.

faqs.q: How late can a deed be filed?
faqs.a: 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. The office itself stays open to 5 p.m., at 1903 Marquette Avenue, Suite A102.
No. Only papers with original signatures are accepted, and a court order must carry the court clerk's certification and seal.

faqs.q: Why two checks at the counter?
faqs.a: The treasurer's $5 certificate for a warranty deed is paid to the Muskegon County Treasurer, separately from the $30 recording fee and any transfer tax.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a sale here?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor. The state charges $3.75 and the county $0.55 for each $500 block of price. Any exemption has to be stated on the deed.

faqs.q: How does a co-owner come off a deed?
faqs.a: By a new, notarized deed that is then recorded. Staff cannot draft it, so use a title company or attorney. A certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a new deed.
